title: Comparable firms for a private bike maker
text: You want to estimate the cost of capital of a private bicycle manufacturer. It has a target debt-to-equity ratio of 0.5. There are no taxes and all debt is risk-free (β_D = 0). The risk-free rate is 3% and the market risk premium 5%.

title: Trident Group: a conglomerate with three divisions
text: Trident Group has three divisions: Food (50% of firm value), Tech (30%) and Energy (20%). It pays no taxes, all debt is risk-free, and Trident's own debt ratio is D/(D + E) = 0.25. The risk-free rate is 3% and the expected market return 9%. Trident has identified one pure-play competitor per division:

title: Brightline: managing the earnings yield
text: Brightline has no debt. Its cash flow (= EBIT = earnings) is EUR 12m this year and is expected to grow at 4% per year forever; all earnings are paid out as dividends. Its market capitalization is EUR 150m and its book equity EUR 90m. It can borrow risk-free at 5% and pays no taxes.

A large shareholder demands a higher earnings yield (earnings / market value of equity). The CFO considers raising the debt-to-equity ratio to 2:1 through a leveraged recapitalization, without changing the assets.
